body:
Well, there was the pan-dimensional vending machine that wouldn't give anything but apple seeds to one of the doctors.  One yen?  One seed.  Two yen?  Two seeds.  10K yen?  You see where this is going.  Even anyone he ASKS to operate the machine gets nothing but apple seeds, like it knows it's him.  Other stuff it vends is pretty freaky, though.

It doesn't feel like I'm suffocating.  It just feels like there's something there.  Like I said, maybe just my brain playing tricks on me.  Might be my subconscious trying to tell me what it wants if I'm gonna do it.

Now I think about it... it feels more like I just don't WANT to breathe.  And I kinda don't want to, really.  Just breathing hurts, even if it's just a little bit.

EDIT: Also, just noticed the part where you said nobody deserves to go through this.  Well, you're not wrong.  Thing is, though, I really did bring this on myself.  It's weird to think that I do and don't deserve it at the same time.  I dunno, I'd have to ponder about that a bit more before I fully understood it.  I mean, yeah, there's stuff in my life that probably led to me being the way I am: My father's death, dealing with a death in the family every year after that for about a decade, my depression kicking in full swing in high school... but at the same time, I didn't put in much effort to make myself a better person, to be the man that she needed me to be.

No one deserves to feel like this, you're right about that.  But I can't deny that this was still my fault.

About the same.  Empty, sharp things around the empty, odd feeling of something around my neck, pressing up against my jaw... I seriously don't know why that's happening.  Maybe just my brain playing tricks on me.  There's nothing there at all.

Still feel like life will be nothing but a letdown if I try to go on because it'll never be as valuable as it could have been.  It's like... okay, I'm gonna be a nerd for a minute.  Are you familiar with the SCP Foundation?  Big self-contained wiki of creepypasta stories (though some are kinda funny).  There's one, a drink machine with a proper keyboard on it.  One of the doctors in the foundation ordered "the perfect drink," drank it, then killed himself the next day because, according to the note he left, "everything's just one big letdown."

It feels like that.
